messages.author: d68a2fc5d13930f4
messages.subject: Trouble running examples provided in the tutorial - "error: ctestConfig1-16.stdout: No such file or directory"
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run some examples provided here (http://iridia.ulb.ac.be/irace/tutorial/index.html#installirace). When I execute the command "checkIraceScenario(scenario=scenario)" in R, I get the following error.


# 2019-05-09 23:11:03 CEST: Checking target execution.
# Executing targetRunner ( 2 times)...
# 2019-05-09 23:11:03 CEST: /home/user/acotsp-example/target-runner testConfig1 16 1234567 /home/user/Instances/tsp-rue-1000-3000/1500-6.tsp --eas --localsearch 0 --alpha 2.2 --beta 3.64 --rho 0.79 --ants 75 --elitistants 177
# 2019-05-09 23:11:03 CEST: ERROR (testConfig1): running command ''/home/user/acotsp-example/target-runner' testConfig1 16 1234567 /home/user/Instances/tsp-rue-1000-3000/1500-6.tsp --eas --localsearch 0 --alpha 2.2 --beta 3.64 --rho 0.79 --ants 75 --elitistants 177 2>&1' had status 1

# Error occurred while executing targetRunner:
== irace == running command ''/home/user/acotsp-example/target-runner' testConfig1 16 1234567 /home/user/Instances/tsp-rue-1000-3000/1500-6.tsp --eas --localsearch 0 --alpha 2.2 --beta 3.64 --rho 0.79 --ants 75 --elitistants 177 2>&1' had status 1
== irace == The call to targetRunner was:
/home/user/acotsp-example/target-runner testConfig1 16 1234567 /home/user/Instances/tsp-rue-1000-3000/1500-6.tsp --eas --localsearch 0 --alpha 2.2 --beta 3.64 --rho 0.79 --ants 75 --elitistants 177
== irace == The output was:
Thu May 9 21:11:03 UTC 2019: error: ctestConfig1-16.stdout: No such file or directory
== irace == This is not a bug in irace, but means that something failed when running the command(s) above or they were terminated before completion. Try to run the command(s) above from the execution directory '/home/user/acotsp-example/exec-dir' to investigate the issue. See also Appendix B (targetRunner troubleshooting checklist) of the User Guide (https://cran.r-project.org/package=irace/vignettes/irace-package.pdf).
# targetRunner returned:
NULL
Error: == irace == Check unsuccessful.

I am not sure what exactly is the error here. Just for your information, I am running R version 3.4.4 (2018-03-15), on Ubuntu 14.04 LTS. The version of irace seems to be v 3.3. Look forward to your reply.

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: Trouble running examples provided in the tutorial - "error: ctestConfig1-16.stdout: No such file or directory"
parts:
Dear Varun,

Apologies, the files used for that tutorial are quite old by now. We need to update them. But it seems that you have updated them (I see you are using target-runner instead of the old hook-run provided in the tutorial).

The error that you see is because something failed when running:

There are many reasons why the command may have failed. Almost always it is a problem with the setup files, permissions or installation, not a bug in irace. Look at the user-guide (as mentioned in the error). There is a step-by-step guide there to find out where the problem is.

If the problem is not something mentioned in the guide, please let us know as we would like to extend the guide in that case.

Best wishes,

Manuel.

messages.author: d68a2fc5d13930f4
messages.subject: Re: Trouble running examples provided in the tutorial - "error: ctestConfig1-16.stdout: No such file or directory"
parts:
Dear Manuel,

I followed the instructions in the manual (v 3.3) to run the ACOTSP example. The first error that I reported was easily solved by editing the variable EXE in target runner. Now, I get an error similar to the one mentioned in Appendix B (3rd point in the checklist). I think the ACOTSP software doesn't print out the objective. Instead, it returns

user@user-ThinkPad-X230:~/tuning$ /home/user/tuning/target-runner 1 35 1779841080 /home/user/tuning/Instances/2000-233.tsp   --ras --localsearch 3 --alpha 1.692 --beta 8.3404 --rho  0.9173 --ants 21 --nnls 15 --dlb 0 --rasranks 17

ACO algorithms for the TSP, v1.03
No options are specified

So, this could definitely be something very specific to the ACOTSP code. I think I will try to tune my algorithm and get back.

Thanks,

Best,
Varun

Hi Varun,

Something in your target-runner is not passing the parameters to ACOTSP correctly. You need to figure out how you are calling it. There is an example target-runner for the ACOTSP in the installation directory. 

Cheers,

Manuel.
